item.content:encoded:
This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.title: News & Events
item.dc:creator: Matias
item.content:encoded:
Finncare news & events

Upcoming Events

Welcome to the news & events page! Here we share all our upcoming events related to Finncare. Below you will find information about our upcoming events.

Finncare Christmas Market

Saturday, November 14, 2026 9am-1pm

Join us at the Finncare Christmas Market on Saturday, 14 November 2026, from 9:00 am–1:00 pm in the Helsinki Room.

Reserve a table: (07) 3829 4800
Location: 343 Cleveland–Redland Bay Rd, Thornlands QLD 4164.

Find out more

Finncare Advance Care Planning Information sessions for EPOAs and Families

Thursday, October, 15 , 2026 10am

Join us on Thursday, 15 October at 10:00 am at Finncare for an information session for EPOAs and families. Learn about Advance Care Planning, Statements of Choices, and the role of an EPOA, with time for Q&A.

Register: info@finncare.org.au | (07) 3829 4800

Find out more

Home Support Services

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible for home support services?

Anyone who is aged 65 or older (or 50+ for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people) and needs support to live safely at home may be eligible. A referral through My Aged Care is typically required.

How do I get started with Finncare's home support?

Contact us directly or call My Aged Care on 1800 200 422. Our team will guide you through the assessment process and match you with the right level of support.

Can I choose my own support worker?

Yes. At Finncare we believe the relationship between client and support worker is important. We do our best to match you with a Finnish-speaking worker and to keep your team consistent.

Got questions?

Our team is ready to answer your questions about home support and help you find the right care.

Tervetuloa
Welcome

Welcome to Finncare

Finncare is an accredited, compassionate provider of aged care and retirement living, based in Thornlands, Queensland. We deliver high-quality care rooted in Finnish and Nordic values — warmth, honesty, respect for nature, and a deep belief in the dignity of every person.

Our doors are open to everyone, regardless of cultural background or language. Whether you are Finnish, Australian, or from anywhere in the world, you will find a genuine community here — one that feels like home.

Discover our services and see how Finncare can support you or someone you love.

Support our community

Stay up to date

Want to work with us?

Donate
News & Events
Work opportunities

What services do we provide?

Want to learn more about us?

Join the Finncare family

Services
Who we are
Contact us

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can access Finncare's services?
Finncare's aged care and retirement living services are open to everyone — you do not need to be of Finnish background. Our services are available to older Australians who meet the standard aged care eligibility criteria, generally aged 65 or older (or 50+ for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people).
How do I apply for a place at Finncare?
To access Australian Government-funded aged care, you first need to register with My Aged Care (myagedcare.gov.au or call 1800 200 422) and complete an ACAT assessment. Once assessed, you can nominate Finncare as your preferred provider. For retirement living, you can contact us directly to arrange a tour and discuss availability.
How much does aged care or retirement living cost?
Costs vary depending on the type of care and your individual financial assessment. Aged care fees in Australia are regulated by the government and are based on your income and assets. A financial assessment through Services Australia (Centrelink) will determine what you pay. We are happy to walk you through the process — contact us for a no-obligation conversation.
Is there a waiting list for housing?
Availability varies depending on the type of accommodation and current occupancy. We encourage you to get in touch early so we can keep you informed of upcoming vacancies and help you plan ahead.

Support Finncare

Finncare relies on the generosity of people who share our belief that everyone deserves dignified, compassionate care. Your support — however large or small — helps us maintain our services, care for our residents, and keep our community connected.
Finncare is a not-for-profit organisation. All donations go directly toward our care and community programs.

Make a donation

item.title: Finnish Community & Culture
item.dc:creator: Tuomas Hartikainen
item.content:encoded:
Finncare is the centre of the Finnish community in Australia. Fostering our unique culture has always been a core of our business. On this page you can see a list of Finnish clubs, churches, media and other community players. Additionally, you can also see their contact details and other handy information.

Embassy of Finland, Canberra

The Embassy’s area of responsibility includes the following countries: Australia, Fiji, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Vanuatu. More information on the Embassy’s activities and other useful information can be found on the country-specific websites and social media.

Email: sanomat.CAN@formin.fi
Phone number: +61 262 733 800

Facebook
Instagram
Twitter

Finnish Radio, Brisbane 98.1FM

Listen live every Wednesday at 5pm & Saturday at 1pm AEST. On radio 98.1FM in South East Queensland or globally online.


Contact information

Email: suomiradio@4eb.org.au

Phone: +61 7 3240 8600

Address: 140 Main Street Kangaroo Point, Brisbane, QLD, Australia

Website

Business Finland Australia

Business Finland is a partner for Finnish companies in international growth. Business Finland in Sydney support companies planning an entry into Australia or seeking to improve their competitiveness in Australia. We help Finnish companies find suitable experts and external consultants, by providing them with objective, market-specific information.

Phone numbers: +61 451 343 379 (Eero Toivainen), +61 41 7790 800 (Hartti Suomela)

Address:

Business Finland Sydney

Level 22, 44 Market Street, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

Finland Australia Chamber of Commerce (FACC)

FACC is a member based business organisation with a focus on facilitating trade and investment between Australia and Finland.

Finland Australia Chamber of Commerce Inc.

T: +61 41 7790 800

E: chamber@finland.com.au

Finnish Community in Queensland

Discover Finnish clubs, churches, support groups and other organisations across Queensland.

Brisbane Finnish Club

Brisbane Finnish Club is the oldest Finnish club in Australia. It was founded initially as a sports club in 1927.

Brisbane Finnish Club organises about 7 events per year. There is also a Finnish library and a little Finnish store at the Finnish House.

Contact information

Address: 62 Newnham Road, Mt. Gravatt East, QLD 4122, Australia

Email: brisfinclub2@gmail.com

Facebook

Finnish Lutheran Church

Pastor Tommi Vuorinen, phone number +61 431 991 250 (in Brisbane)

Chairman Matti Hirvelä +61 402 961 300

Secretary Kyllikki Havukainen +61 408 936 612

Additionally, we recommend English services at St Andrew’s church (25 Wickham Tce, Brisbane City) every Sunday at 10am. These services are mostly conducted by our Finnish Pastor Tommi.

If you need a Pastor for a baptism, a wedding or a funeral, please contact Tommi directly.

Sunshine Coast Finnish Friends Support

Founded 15.5.2011 (not incorporated)

Contact person:  Elli Hentunen

Phone number: +61 418 263 530

 Email address: ekhentunen@gmail.com

Sunshine Coast Finnish Friends Support (SCFFS) is a volunteer based support group for aging people of Finnish background living on the Sunshine Coast.  

We provide culturally and linguistically appropriate support assisting people to live independently longer in their own homes and to enjoy interacting with the wider community thus enhancing their quality of life.

GOLD COAST FINNISH SPORT CLUB

Contact details

Chairperson: Allan Ratilainen +61 402 100 351

Secretary: Kristy Nyrhinen +61 402 249 867

Email: gcfsc@outlook.com

Facebook

History

GCFSC was started on the 22/1/1978. Hundreds of Finnish migrants were living on the Gold Coast due to the building industry. Finns were renowned for their formwork skills. GCFSC started with volleyball in the park every Sunday and Pesapallo began in 1982 when the Club first hosted the Annual Finnish Festival.

Each Sunday was a “kentta” day and every 3 months there would be a dance held with a Finnish band and dancing. The club first participated at the annual Finnish Easter Festival in Mt Isa in 1980 and have had participants at each Easter Festival since. The GCFSC have hosted these Festivals 5 times; 1982, 1996, 2003, 2010, 2019.  The Club also hosted the Pesapallo World Cup in 2012, with players travelling from countries such as Finland, Germany and Switzerland.

The current sporting focus of the Club is on Pesapallo and Molkky. On the first Wednesday of each month, there is a picnic at the Botanical Gardens in Benowa. This is to continue the social circle for the older generation, but of course, everyone is welcome.

The GCFSC host an annual Christmas Lunch/Dinner with traditional Finnish Christmas foods prepared entirely by volunteers. Membership benefits of the Club include an annual Club Lunch, as well as financial aid to participants competing at interstate Finnish Easter Games.

FINNISH CULTURE

Where…

The Republic of Finland, is a Nordic country situated in the Northern Europe. It is bordered by Sweden to the west, Norway to the north, Russia to the east, and Estonia to the south across the Gulf of Finland.

Population…

At the end of year 2019, 5.5 million people called Finland home, with the majority concentrated in its southern regions. About one million residents live in the Greater Helsinki area (consisting of Helsinki, Espoo, Kauniainen, and Vantaa) and a third of the country’s GDP is produced there. Other larger cities include Tampere, Turku, Oulu, Jyväskylä, Lahti, and Kuopio.

Size / Area…

On the map compared to Australia, Finland seems to be quite small country but actually it is the eighth largest country in Europe and the most sparsely populated country in the European Union. Finland has an area of 338,424 km2.

Climate…

Seasons in Finland are completely opposite to what we have here in Australia. When Australia is sweltering on hot summer days, Finland is experiencing the coldest time of the year.

Winters of southern Finland (when mean daily temperature remains below 0 °C) are usually about 100 days long, and the snow typically covers the land from about late November to mid-April. Even in the most temperate regions of the south, the harshest winter nights can see the temperatures fall to −30 °C. Climatic summers (when mean daily temperature remains above 10 °C) in southern Finland last from about late May to mid-September, and in the inland, the warmest days of July can reach 38 °C.

In northern Finland, particularly in Lapland, the winters are long and cold, while the summers are relatively warm but short. The most severe winter days in Lapland can see the temperature fall down to −45 °C. The winter of the north lasts for about 200 days with permanent snow cover from about mid-October to early May. Summers in the north are quite short, only two to three months, but can still see maximum daily temperatures above 25 °C during heat waves.

A quarter of Finland’s territory lies within the Arctic Circle and the midnight sun can be experienced for more days the farther north one travels. At Finland’s northernmost point, the sun does not set for 73 consecutive days during summer, and does not rise at all for 51 days during winter.

Quick Facts…

item.content:encoded:
Finncare prides itself on maintaining high quality standards and providing the best service to those in our care. Whilst the Federal Government contributes substantially towards care of our residents and clients, it is vitally important  for us to fundraise to improve current facilities, replace capital items and purchase much needed equipment to enhance the lives of those we care for.

By making a donation and/or bequest, you will enable Finncare to do more for our residents and clients, providing extras and amenities that cannot be supplied via the normal funding from Government. Your donation or bequest will continue to make a real positive difference to those that receive Finncare services.

All money raised by Donations or Bequests is used to improve current facilities or make capital purchases.  Our commitment to you is to ensure your gift will be administered and applied in accordance with your expressed wishes and duly acknowledged with our thanks.

Make a Donation

Donations to Finncare can make a lasting difference to how we provide care and amenities for our residents and Finncare clients. Any donation, large or small, can mean new wheelchairs, improved facilities, better activities and a more comprehensive community of care.

To make a donation please contact our Administration Coordinator on 07 3829 4800 who will send you a form or you can make your donation directly via credit card.

  • Call 07 3829 4800 to make a donation via credit card

Donations of $2 or more are tax deductible. Please talk to us about where you want your donation directed and how we can recognise your valued support.

Make a Bequest

Through a bequest to Finncare, you can leave a lasting legacy to the care of our elderly Finnish community and benefit current and future generations.

A Bequest is a gift made through a Will, testamentary trust, or codicil, to a Will or trust. Bequests may include cash, marketable securities, closely held stock, real estate or other personal property.

If you would like to discuss the idea of a bequest with us in more detail, please phone our Administration Coordinator on 07 3829 4800 or email generalmanager@finncare.org.au. Together we can find an appropriate way to acknowledge your contribution so others are aware of your care and consideration of others in our community.

item.title: Our People
item.dc:creator: Sachet
item.content:encoded:
Behind every service, there is a team of dedicated professionals working to make a difference.

Board Members

Katriina Tähkä

Miselle Pons

Anna Rofhoek-Bjoerni

President

Vice President

Treasurer

Katriina Tähkä holds a Bachelor of Arts & Bachelor of Laws and has specialised in employment law. She has more than 20 years experience advising businesses on strategic people management and resolving workplace issues. Katriina was born in Sydney to Finnish parents and is a dual citizen as are her children. Katriina has a strong commitment to her Finnish background and culture and to ensuring that all communities are inclusive of different cultures and people. Her previous Board experience was helping new migrants feel welcome in Australia.

Miselle Pons holds Diploma in Law (LPAB) from University of Sydney and Master of Laws (LLM) from Finland. She has extensive e xperience in strategic support and legal, governance and risk & compliance aspects of complex businesses. Miselle was born in Northern Finland, and moved to Sydney in 2008. She changed her career in 2022 and has since executed her dream of creating her own brand inspired by the long drink culture in Finland. She is now a passionate start-up owner of a beverage company Kippis Drinks. Miselle has served as an Executive Committee Member of Finland Australia Chamber of Commerce Inc. Miselle has twin children who were born in Finland. They are her greatest mentors in modern progressive society. Miselle and her children are dual citizens and share a strong bond with their family and roots back in Finland.

Anna grew up in Närpiö, Finland and lived most recently in Espoo. Anna and her family moved to Sydney in 2020 and settled on the Northern Beaches. She has a Bachelor of Commerce from Flinders University and a Masters in Economics from the Swedish School of Economics in Helsinki (Hanken). She has vast financial management and reporting experience spanning various industries such as hospitality, chemicals and telecommunications. She is currently working as Financial Controller at Altora Ag (the largest cropping producer in Australia). She is passionate about delivering value and excellence to the organisations she works with. Anna and her family enjoy travelling and visit Finland as often as possible.


Petra Lappalainen

Dr Juhani Tuovinen

Mirja Roti

Board member

Board member

Board member

Petra Lappalainen hails from Helsinki, Finland, but has lived in New York and Melbourne for almost 30 years in total.

Petra is a finance leader with a 20+ year track record of successfully delivering results in risk management, banking product development, management consulting, and project management.

She is passionate about:

  • advising businesses on identifying and mitigating financial and operational risk;
  • transforming businesses to embrace strategic or regulatory changes; and
  • developing and mentoring staff to reach their potential.

Dr Juhani Tuovinen was born in Tervo, Finland, and emigrated to Australia with his family in 1960. He is a dual citizen currently residing in Adelaide. He holds Bachelors, Masters and doctoral degrees in Education. After initially working as a teacher in three states of Australia, his subsequent work in higher education involved teaching, industry engagement and research. He has held professorial level positions in both public and private higher education and brings board experience from multiple contexts to Finncare. In his retirement he continues to hold an Adjunct Professor position at the Sheridan Institute of Higher Education, Perth, his most recent full-time professorial work context. He has been and continues to be associated with the Australian Finnish Pentecostal church as well as having conducted research for the Australian Lutheran College and Australian Lutheran schools. He considers it a privilege to contribute to the welfare of Finnish migrants by serving on the Finncare Board.

Mirja Roti migrated to Sydney in 1974. She was a qualified cook, but decided to begin a nursing career as an Assistant in Nursing at a facility in Rooty Hill. She moved to Canberra, where she studied to become an Enrolled Nurse, and later became a qualified Registered Nurse in 2003. She worked with elderly residents in aged care settings for over 20 years, and spent the last 20 years as a neonatal nurse. Mirja enjoys working with the elderly – for a time, she was travelling a 250km round trip to provide assistance with shopping, doctors appointments and general companionship to an elderly Finnish lady. Mirja is now retired, but keeps herself busy – she loves to bake (and makes a mean ruisleipä!) and has made dozens of patchwork quilts. She travels to Finland once a year to see her 92 year old father.

Leadership team

Dr. Leena Vuorinen

Mewan Silva

Ushani Siriwardhana

Chief Executive Officer

Senior Financial Accountant

Clinical Manager

Dr. Leena Vuorinen brings over 30 years of leadership experience in aged care, both in residential and community-based services. Most recently, she served as the General Manager of Aging Services at Deaf Connect, where she was responsible for delivering high-quality, customer-centered services across multiple states. Throughout her career, Leena has driven innovations in aged care, strengthened staff competencies, and fostered a culture of continuous development. She holds a PhD in Social Policy, specializing in aging research, as well as a postgraduate qualification in Community Sector Management. Leena also serves as the Chair of the Board of Lutheran Services, which reflects her strong commitment to good governance and the well-being of the community.

Senior Financial Accountant Mewan Silva is an experienced finance professional with over 18 years of experience in Aged Care, Child Care, Community Sector Development, Public Sectors and Manufacturing. He is a member of CPA Australia and the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA) in the UK. He holds a Bachelor of Business Administration.

Ushani completed a Bachelor of Nursing at QUT, where she developed a strong foundation in clinical practice. After becoming a Registered Nurse in Aged Care, she advanced to Clinical Nurse and then Clinical Manager, working with a range of aged care organizations from small to large. Ushani has a hands-on and compassionate approach to leadership of the RAC nursing team. She holds a focus on improving resident care and supporting clinical teams and believes in creating an environment where both staff and residents thrive.

Other Key Personnel

Amy Piekkala-Fletcher

Dr Ritva Eronen

Secretary

Public Officer

Over the past 20 years, Amy has managed projects across a variety of industries, in the private, academic and public sectors. She is currently a Construction Project Manager at Seqwater, South East Queensland’s bulk water supplier. She manages projects implemented to maintain and build new water infrastructure. She holds a Bachelor of Media and Communication, a Graduate Certificate of Integrated Water Management and a Certificate IV in Project Management. Amy has been a member of the Finncare Board since 2016. She recently consulted to Finncare as the Villa Project Manager, undertaking capital works to rejuvenate the Villas. Amy is born and bred in Brisbane, of a Finnish mother and an Australian father.
